title: Committee of Supply – Head N (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head N (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

sections.label: Global COVID-19 cases and South Korea
sections.summary: COVID-19 has infected 88,000 people and killed over 3,000 worldwide, with South Korea the biggest nest of infection outside China.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Just today, Channel NewsAsia reported that the global COVID-19 death toll now exceeds 3,000, with 88,0000 people infected worldwide across 60 countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: South Korea has now become the biggest nest of infection outside China, with more than 4,000 cases in total.

sections.label: Malaysia and Indonesia COVID-19 testing
sections.summary: Malaysia has few cases and Indonesia none, possibly because they cannot do the large-scale testing Singapore has done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Malaysia has a small number of cases and Indonesia has not detected any yet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: However, part of the reason for this small number in some of these countries may have been because they are unable to do the large-scale testing that Singapore has engaged in.

sections.label: Singapore COVID-19 response praised
sections.summary: Singapore's way of dealing with COVID-19 has won praise from the World Health Organization.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore's way of dealing with COVID-19 has won praise from the World Health Organization.

sections.label: Muhyiddin Yassin sworn in
sections.summary: Yesterday, Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin was sworn in as the eighth Prime Minister of Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Yesterday, Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin was sworn in as the eighth Prime Minister of Malaysia.

sections.label: Johor River pollution incidents
sections.summary: Since 2017, seven pollution incidents in the Johor River catchment shut down PUB's Johor waterworks, disrupting raw water supply to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On pollution, since 2017, there have been seven incidents affecting the Johor River which shut down the Public Utilities Board's (PUB's) Johor waterworks, disrupting the supply of raw water to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: That arose because of illegal discharges within the water catchment area from industries, such as chicken farms and palm oil mills in particular, and pollution in general.

sections.label: Johor water reserves and tariffs
sections.summary: Malaysian leaders said Johor's water reserve threshold will drop to zero, and a commission proposed raising water tariffs by 10% to 20%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In Johor, senior Malaysian leaders also shared last year that by the second half of this year, Johor's water reserve threshold will drop down to zero, and alluded that Malaysia would have to look after the interests of Malaysians first.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: More broadly, the Malaysian National Water Services Commission has proposed that Malaysian states should look to increase water tariffs by 10% to 20%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The fact that Singapore has, in turn, locked the low price of treated water sold to around 11 sen per 1,000 litres and supplied more water to Malaysia than required under the existing water agreement is likely to remain a footnote.

sections.label: Singapore-Brunei ties and cooperation
sections.summary: The Currency Interchangeability Agreement and defence cooperation underpin robust Singapore-Brunei ties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Currency Interchangeability Agreement and our strong defence cooperation underpin the robust ties between Singapore and Brunei.

sections.label: President Halimah's Brunei visit
sections.summary: During her May 2018 visit, President Halimah mentioned possible cooperation areas and witnessed two financial pacts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: During President Halimah’s visit in May 2018, she mentioned that possible areas of cooperation included eco-tourism, aquaculture and financial technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The President also witnessed the signing of two pacts to strengthen financial cooperation between our two countries.

sections.label: US-Singapore trade ranking
sections.summary: In 2019, the US was Singapore's third largest goods trading partner and top services trading partner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: In 2019, the US was Singapore’s third largest trading partner in goods and top trading partner in services.

sections.label: US military facilities access extension
sections.summary: A Protocol of Amendment extended the 1990 Memorandum of Understanding on US access to Singapore's military facilities by 15 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: A Protocol of Amendment signed between Prime Minister Lee and President Trump extended the 1990 Memorandum of Understanding, which covers the US' access to Singapore's military facilities, for another 15 years.

sections.label: US State Department ASEAN assessment
sections.summary: The US State Department assessed ASEAN as commanding greater Asia Pacific influence than members individually, especially Singapore in the 1960s and 1970s.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: Indeed, the US State Department's assessment of ASEAN is that ASEAN commands far greater influence on the Asia Pacific trade, political and security issues than its members could achieve individually and, for all of the ASEAN member nations, this was particularly true of Singapore in the 1960s and 1970s.

sections.label: MFA update on ASEAN progress
sections.summary: A question asks MFA for an update on ASEAN progress, including centrality, the South China Sea Code of Conduct and the common market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Chairman, can MFA provide an update on the key ASEAN progress and developments in the past year, including updates on issues, such as upholding ASEAN centrality, developing the Code of Conduct for the South China Sea, and fostering the ASEAN common market?

sections.label: ASEAN middle-class market growth
sections.summary: By 2030, 60% of the population will be middle-class, making ASEAN the fourth largest single market after the US, China and the EU.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: By 2030, 60% of the population will be middle-class and thus ASEAN will be the fourth largest single market in the world after the US, China and the European Union (EU).

sections.label: COVID-19 supply chain disruption
sections.summary: The recent COVID-19 outbreak has shown how disruption of supply chain can have global impact on trade.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: The recent COVID-19 outbreak has shown just how one key aspect, the disruption of supply chain, can have global impact on trade.

sections.label: MFA engagement with regional partners
sections.summary: The speaker asks how MFA intends to strengthen engagement with key partners in the region to keep Singapore a relevant stakeholder.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: In this regard, I would like to ask how MFA intends to strengthen our engagement with such key partners in the region to ensure that Singapore remains a relevant stakeholder.

sections.label: Humanitarian help for refugees
sections.summary: The speaker says this is not a political issue or interference in domestic affairs, but a humanitarian disaster, and help should be provided to over a million refugees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This is not a political issue and we are not interfering with domestic affairs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This is a humanitarian disaster and we can and should provide help to over a million refugees.

sections.label: Commuters crossing Causeway border
sections.summary: An estimated 250,000 commuters cross the border at the Causeway daily, with more movement via the Tuas Second Link and by air.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For example, an estimated 250,000 commuters cross the border at the Causeway daily and, in addition, we have more movement via the Tuas Second Link and also by air.

sections.label: Asia-Ready Exposure programme target
sections.summary: The Government announced the Asia-Ready Exposure programme and set the "70-70" target to increase youths' exposure to ASEAN.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Government has announced the Asia-Ready Exposure programme and set the "70-70" target to increase our youths' exposure to ASEAN.

sections.label: Singapore cybersecurity UN ASEAN
sections.summary: Singapore is a member of the UNGGE set up in 2004, and the ASEAN-Singapore Cybersecurity Centre of Excellence was set up last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For example, Singapore is a member of the United Nations (UN) Group of Government Experts (UNGGE) which was set up in 2004 aimed at forging a common set of norms and rules of cyberspace amongst UN members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Last year, we saw the setting up of the ASEAN-Singapore Cybersecurity Centre of Excellence.

sections.label: IPCC 1.5C warming report
sections.summary: The 2018 IPCC report concluded the 1.5°C threshold will be breached between 2030 and 2052 and current pledges are consistent with 3°C warming.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The 2018 Inter-governmental Panel on Climate Change Special Report on the effects of global warming of 1.5°C concluded that at the current warming rates, this 1.5°C threshold will be breached between 2030 and 2052, and that the current ambition level of countries' climate pledges is insufficient and only consistent with a 3°C warming pathway.

sections.label: China Singapore trading partners
sections.summary: China has been Singapore's largest trading partner since 2013 and Singapore is China's largest foreign investor.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Chairman, China has been Singapore's largest trading partner since 2013 and Singapore is China's largest foreign investor.

sections.label: Tianjin Eco-city companies residents
sections.summary: The Tianjin Eco-city features 8,200 registered companies and over 100,000 people living and working in its 30 square kilometre area.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Tianjin Eco-city also now features 8,200 registered companies and over 100,000 people living and working in its 30 square kilometre area.

sections.label: Singapore firms China supply chain
sections.summary: Firms in Singapore with partners and supply chain parts in China experienced work stoppage and difficulty moving products in and out of China.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Anecdotally, firms in Singapore which have partners and parts of the supply chain based in China have experienced work stoppage and difficulty in moving products in and out of China.

sections.label: Singapore China bilateral agreements
sections.summary: At the 15th Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation, Singapore and China inked nine agreements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: At the 15th Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation, Singapore and China have inked nine agreements.

sections.label: Singapore-China diplomatic relations anniversary
sections.summary: 2020 marks 30 years of Singapore-China formal diplomatic relations, with both countries investing significantly and enterprises venturing out together.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Twenty-twenty marks the 30th anniversary of Singapore-China formal diplomatic relations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Our two countries have come a long way, achieving many important milestones, whilst enduring moments that tested the strength and depth of our relations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Over the decades, our economies developed our unique capabilities and character.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We invest in each other significantly and enterprises from Singapore and China are also venturing out together.

sections.label: Younger leaders engaging Chinese leaders
sections.summary: A question asks what plan exists for Singapore's younger leaders to build on current relations and deepen ties with Chinese leaders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: As such, what is the plan for Singapore’s younger leaders to build on our current strong relations to deepen their relations with Chinese leaders?

sections.label: MFA engaging Singaporeans on foreign policy
sections.summary: A question asks what MFA efforts exist to engage Singaporeans on the fundamentals of Singapore's foreign policy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: What are MFA’s efforts to engage Singaporeans on the fundamentals of Singapore’s foreign policy?

sections.label: Singapore-Australia cultural cooperation
sections.summary: Singapore and Australia agreed to strengthen cultural cooperation, establishing an arts group and a fund of up to S$5 million over five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For instance, Singapore and Australia have agreed to strengthen cultural cooperation by building on the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) on Arts and Culture that both countries signed in June 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We have established an Australia-Singapore Arts Group to increase collaboration between our artists, arts groups and cultural institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MFA and the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) jointly established a fund of up to S$5 million over a period of five years to support Singapore artists, arts groups and performers to profile their works in Australia.

sections.label: Nine agreements signed by countries
sections.summary: Both countries signed nine agreements covering customs clearance, IP management, education, innovation, communications and smart city development, and exchanged views on relations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Both countries signed nine agreements, which covered areas like customs clearance, IP management, education, innovation and communications, as well as smart city development, and exchange views on "excellent" state of relations back in October last year.

sections.label: Cultural diplomacy and soft power
sections.summary: A speaker urges the Government to turn MOUs with foreign partners into action plans to expand Singapore's cultural soft power.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Through cultural diplomacy, Singapore can project global influence and enhance relations with our foreign partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, I urge the Government to explore further and perhaps turn the signing of MOUs with our foreign partners into concrete and solid action plans, an instrumental role in expanding Singapore's cultural soft power to increase our presence and space.

sections.label: Flights bringing Singaporeans home from Wuhan
sections.summary: Two flights to Wuhan in late January and early February brought home 266 Singaporeans and family members from Hubei Province.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Members will know that we launched two flights in late-January and early-February this year to Wuhan to bring our people home.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: There was a total of 266 Singaporeans and their family members from Hubei Province in China who returned.

sections.label: Singapore aid to China during crisis
sections.summary: Singapore sent testing equipment, test kits, protective equipment and medical supplies to Wuhan, and the Singapore Red Cross raised over $6 million for affected communities in China.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: He expressed his gratitude for our efforts to support China during this crisis.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We sent testing equipment and test kits which were developed in Singapore to Wuhan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We also sent personal protective equipment and other medical supplies that were needed because of the sheer scale of the challenges that they were facing in Wuhan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The Singapore Red Cross has raised more than $6 million for the affected communities across China, and we have been working together with the international community to address this emerging global epidemic, and some people would say, pandemic.

sections.label: Muhyiddin Yassin appointed Malaysia's Prime Minister
sections.summary: Singapore congratulates Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin on being appointed Malaysia's eighth Perdana Menteri after political developments across the Causeway.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Members would be aware, of course, of the ongoing major political developments just across the Causeway last week.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We congratulate Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin on being appointed Malaysia's eighth Perdana Menteri.

sections.label: Singapore-Malaysia relations and joint projects
sections.summary: Singapore hopes for a constructive relationship with Malaysia and looks forward to resuming discussions on issues and projects including the RTS and HSR.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We hope we will continue to have a constructive, mutually beneficial relationship with Malaysia and we look forward to resuming the discussions on the ongoing issues and projects which Members are all aware of.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We have always sought a win-win approach in the many areas where we have common interests, such as the Singapore-Johor Bahru Rapid Transit System (RTS) and the Singapore-Kuala Lumpur High Speed Rail (HSR).

sections.label: Malaysia lost right to review water price
sections.summary: Singapore's long-standing position is that Malaysia lost the right to review the water price under 62WA, told to Malaysia as early as 2002.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Singapore's position, a long-standing position which successive Foreign Ministers have reiterated, is that Malaysia has lost the right to review the price of water under 62WA, and we had told Malaysia this, as early as 2002, when Singapore last negotiated with Malaysia on water as part of a package deal.

sections.label: Review of raw and treated water prices
sections.summary: Singapore told Malaysia that reviewing the raw water price also means reviewing the treated water price sold to Johor, and both sides must discuss Johor River water yield and quality.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: I believe we met in December 2019 and January 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We made it clear to Malaysia that any review of the price of raw water sold to Singapore will also mean a review of the price of treated water sold to Johor.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Both sides must also discuss the yield and the quality of the water from the Johor River, so as to ensure that Singapore can continue to draw our entitlement of 250 million gallons per day of raw water under the 62WA for the remaining 41 years of the Water Agreement.

sections.label: 1990 Water Agreement and Linggiu Reservoir
sections.summary: The 1990 Water Agreement led to the Linggiu Reservoir, completed in 1993, to ensure sustainable abstraction of 250 million gallons per day from the Johor River.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Emeritus Senior Minister Goh Chok Tong was just sharing with me just now that, in fact, the two of them had a final round of negotiations in what was then the NOL Penthouse.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: This 1990 Water Agreement led to the construction of the Linggiu Reservoir that was completed in 1993 to ensure the sustainable abstraction of our entitlement of 250 million gallons per day of raw water from the Johor River.

sections.label: Barrage operational, more needed
sections.summary: The barrage became fully operational in March 2017, but much more needs to be done urgently.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The barrage became fully operational in March 2017 but, let me be frank, much more needs to be done and to be done urgently.

sections.label: PUB supplies Johor treated water
sections.summary: PUB has continued out of good will to provide additional treated water to Johor at 50 sen per thousand gallons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: PUB, out of good will, has continued to provide this additional treated water to Johor at the same price of 50 sen per thousand gallons.

sections.label: Johor raw water obligations consequences
sections.summary: If Johor cannot fulfil its Water Agreement obligation to provide 250 million gallons of raw water, there will be grave consequences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: If Johor is unable to fulfil its obligations to provide us with 250 million gallons of raw water, as stipulated by the Water Agreement, this will have grave consequences.

sections.label: Arbitration if negotiations fail
sections.summary: If Singapore and Malaysia cannot reach an amicable outcome through negotiations, Singapore is prepared to resolve issues through arbitration on mutually agreed terms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: So, Mr Pritam Singh's comments just now are entirely consonant with the position that we are taking.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: However, if despite our best efforts Singapore and Malaysia are unable to reach an amicable outcome on these issues through negotiations, then Singapore is prepared to resolve them through arbitration on terms mutually agreed to by both countries.

sections.label: Singapore-Indonesia framework on sensitive issues
sections.summary: Singapore and Indonesia agreed on a framework providing a basis for discussion on managing the Flight Information Region and military training.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: As the two leaders announced at the Leaders' Retreat last year, Singapore and Indonesia have agreed on a framework which provides a sound and comprehensive basis for discussion on two sensitive issues – the management of our Flight Information Region and military training.

sections.label: Talks on Singapore-Indonesia issues
sections.summary: No deadline is set for the talks, which will follow international law, Indonesia's sovereignty, Singapore's training rights and Changi's needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: No deadline has been set for the conclusion of these talks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We will address these issues in accordance with: first, international law, including the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), International Civil Aviation Authority Rules, International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) rules and provisions; second, respect for Indonesia's sovereignty over its territory; third, respect for Singapore's long-standing rights to conduct military training in accordance with UNCLOS; fourth, the long-term needs of Changi Airport.

sections.label: US-Singapore defence MOU renewal
sections.summary: Prime Minister Lee met President Trump in New York last September and they signed a renewal of the 1990 defence cooperation MOU.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Prime Minister Lee met President Donald Trump in New York last September and Members will recall from the earlier discussion that they signed a renewal of the 1990 MOU on defence cooperation between our two countries.

sections.label: US investment stock in Singapore
sections.summary: In 2018 US investment stock in Singapore was S$289 billion, making Singapore the largest Asian recipient of US FDI.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In 2018, the United States' investment stock in Singapore stood at S$289 billion, making us, in fact, the largest recipient of US foreign direct investments (FDIs) in Asia.

sections.label: Singapore-China government projects and investment
sections.summary: Singapore's G-to-G projects in Suzhou, Tianjin and Chongqing reflect its role in China's development, and Singapore has been China's largest foreign investor since 2013.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Our government-to-government (G-to-G) projects in Suzhou, Tianjin and Chongqing are icons of success that reflect Singapore’s complementary role at various phases of China’s spectacular development.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: And even though we are so small, Singapore has been China’s largest foreign investor since 2013.

sections.label: US options for dealing with China
sections.summary: The US can work with China within a rules-based system and compete fairly, or seek dominance and arrange rules to limit China's power.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The US has to decide how to deal with China.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: It can work with China in the global order, get China to participate within a rules-based system and compete with China on a fair basis, or the US can strive to remain the dominant power in all arenas, in all areas at all costs and seek to arrange international rules so as to limit China's power and influence.

sections.label: Singapore avoiding choosing sides
sections.summary: Singapore must avoid choosing sides, deepen cooperation with both China and the US, and encourage all parties to follow international law.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: While Singapore may find ourselves squeezed in the middle, we must avoid choosing sides.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Instead, we must find ways to deepen and enhance our cooperation with both China and the US, including in new areas of mutual interest, and encourage all parties to act in accordance with international law.

sections.label: Principled action for Singapore Citizens
sections.summary: Singapore acts in a principled way and does only what is in the best long-term interests of Singapore Citizens.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Ultimately, we act in a principled way and will only do what is in the best long-term interests of Singapore Citizens.

sections.label: Diplomacy to protect sovereignty
sections.summary: Distressed citizens overseas have a home to return to, so Singapore must invest a fair share of resources in diplomacy to protect sovereignty and keep Singaporeans safe.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: And it means our distressed citizens overseas have a country, a city-state and a home to come back to.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We must thus continue to invest a fair share of our resources in diplomacy, so that we have the capacity to protect our sovereignty and, most importantly, keep Singapore and Singaporeans safe.

sections.label: South China Sea COC negotiations
sections.summary: The First Reading of the Single Draft Negotiating Text for the South China Sea Code of Conduct was completed last year and the Second Reading has started.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Mr Henry Kwek asked about the progress of the negotiations on the Code of Conduct in the South China Sea (COC).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We completed the First Reading of the Single Draft Negotiating Text for the COC last year and have started on the Second Reading.

sections.label: Humanitarian aid to Bangladesh and Myanmar
sections.summary: Singapore has contributed over S$1 million in bilateral humanitarian aid to Bangladesh and Myanmar.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: To reply to Mr Louis Ng's query, Singapore has contributed over S$1 million in bilateral humanitarian aid to Bangladesh and Myanmar.

sections.label: ASEAN FDI inflows in 2018
sections.summary: In 2018, total FDI inflows into ASEAN amounted to some US$155 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In 2018, total FDI inflows into ASEAN amounted to some US$155 billion.

sections.label: Singapore largest ASEAN exporter and importer
sections.summary: In 2018, Singapore was the region's largest exporter and importer, accounting for 28.8% of ASEAN exports and 26.8% of imports.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In 2018, Singapore was the largest exporter and importer of the region, accounting for 28.8% and 26.8% of ASEAN exports and imports, respectively.

sections.label: ASEAN visitor arrivals growth
sections.summary: Visitor arrivals to ASEAN reached 135 million in 2018, an estimated 264% increase from 2005, with Singapore consistently among the top ASEAN countries.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Visitor arrivals to ASEAN have increased markedly, reaching 135 million in 2018, an estimated 264% increase from 2005, and Singapore is consistently among the top ASEAN countries with highest visitor arrivals.

sections.label: Singapore-Indonesia economic cooperation
sections.summary: Economic cooperation includes Kendal Industrial Park and Nongsa Digital Park, Singapore has been Indonesia's top foreign investor since 2014, and agreements will increase trade once ratified.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Our economic cooperation continues to grow from strength to strength through flagship collaborative projects, including the Kendal Industrial Park project in Central Java and Nongsa Digital Park project in Batam.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We have been Indonesia's top foreign investor since 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The updated Avoidance of Double Taxation Agreement, which was signed during President Halimah Yacob's State Visit to Indonesia in February, along with our Bilateral Investment Treaty, will further increase two-way trade and investments once the agreements are ratified.

sections.label: Singapore-Philippines MOUs concluded
sections.summary: During President Halimah Yacob's State Visit to the Philippines, Singapore and the Philippines concluded eight MOUs on data protection, data innovation and smart city infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: For instance, during President Halimah Yacob's State Visit to the Philippines in September last year, Singapore and the Philippines concluded eight MOUs that chart cooperation in emerging areas like data protection, data innovation and smart city infrastructure.

sections.label: SAYF funding addition
sections.summary: Singapore added S$5 million to the SAYF during its 2018 ASEAN Chairmanship to promote leadership development, community service and entrepreneurship amongst ASEAN youths.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Singapore added S$5 million to the SAYF during our 2018 ASEAN Chairmanship to promote leadership development, community service and entrepreneurship amongst ASEAN youths.

sections.label: Paris Agreement commitments enhancement
sections.summary: Singapore will enhance its Nationally Determined Contribution and submit a long-term low emissions development strategy for 2050.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Mr Amrin Amin asked how we are fulfilling our Paris Agreement commitments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We will enhance our Nationally Determined Contribution and submit a long-term low emissions development strategy for 2050.

sections.label: Southeast Asia defence cooperation
sections.summary: Southeast Asia has robust defence and security cooperation through joint exercises such as the Sulu-Sulawesi Straits Patrol and the Malacca Straits Patrol.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Within Southeast Asia, there is robust defence and security cooperation through joint exercises, such as the Sulu-Sulawesi Straits Patrol and the Malacca Straits Patrol.

sections.label: Abu Dhabi and Gulf visits
sections.summary: Singapore hosted Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Al Nahyan and signed a comprehensive partnership declaration; President Halimah Yacob visited Saudi Arabia and Kuwait.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In February last year, we hosted an official visit by Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Al Nahyan and signed a joint declaration on comprehensive partnership.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: President Halimah Yacob also made a historic State Visit to Saudi Arabia and Kuwait in November 2019.

sections.label: Saudi umrah visa suspension
sections.summary: Singapore hopes Saudi Arabia's temporary umrah visa suspension, a COVID-19 precaution, will be lifted so Singaporeans can perform umrah safely.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: On the temporary suspension of umrah visas by the Saudi Government as a precautionary measure in view of the COVID-19 outbreak, Singapore hopes that the suspension will be lifted in due course so that Singaporeans can proceed with their umrah in a safe and secure manner.

sections.label: Singapore-China diplomatic relations anniversary
sections.summary: Singapore and China are marking the 30th anniversary of the establishment of their diplomatic relations this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Chairman, we are celebrating the 30th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Singapore and China this year.

sections.label: Singapore-China bilateral MOUs signed
sections.summary: Singapore and China signed nine bilateral MOUs and agreements covering trade, finance, culture, the environment and a youth internship exchange programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Singapore and China had then signed nine bilateral MOUs and agreements, ranging from trade, finance, culture, the environment and a youth internship exchange programme.

sections.label: China-Singapore trade and investment
sections.summary: Since 2013, China has been Singapore's largest trading partner and Singapore has been China's largest foreign investor.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Since 2013, China has been Singapore's largest trading partner, and Singapore has been China's largest foreign investor.

sections.label: Singapore aid to China
sections.summary: The Singapore Government gave S$1 million seed funding and donated medical supplies and test kits to China; the Singapore Red Cross appeal raised over S$6 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: On our part, the Singapore Government contributed S$1 million as seed funding to catalyse the Singapore Red Cross' public appeal to raise funds to help our Chinese friends, and donated medical supplies and diagnostic test kits to China.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: The Singapore Red Cross’ fundraising drive has received support from our trade associations and chambers, companies and local community organisations, as well as members of the public, and has raised more than S$6 million to date.

sections.label: Singapore-India economic cooperation
sections.summary: Singapore is India's largest foreign investor and cooperation is expanding into innovation, digital economy and FinTech, refreshing the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Our relationship with India presents continuing opportunities for Singaporeans and our businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: We are the largest foreign investor in India and many of our local companies have expanded there.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: With both countries making strides towards digitalisation, our cooperation is expanding to cover new frontiers, such as innovation, digital economy and FinTech.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: We are exploring new areas of cooperation to refresh our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (CSP).

sections.label: EU-Singapore agreements signed
sections.summary: The EU-Singapore FTA, Investment Protection Agreement and Partnership and Cooperation Agreement were signed in 2018, with the FTA in force in November.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: A major milestone was the signing of the EU-Singapore FTA (EUSFTA), the EU-Singapore Investment Protection Agreement, as well as the EU-Singapore Partnership and Cooperation Agreement in 2018, and the EUSFTA’s entry into force in November last year.

sections.label: Nationalist sentiments eroding multilateralism
sections.summary: Rising nationalist, isolationist and protectionist sentiments erode support for globalisation and multilateralism, affecting free trade norms and international law important to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: Indeed, the deepening mood of nationalist, isolationist and protectionist sentiments in many countries is eroding support for globalisation and multilateralism.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: This matters for us because it can affect global norms on free trade and international law, both of which are integral to Singapore's survival as a small nation-state.

sections.label: Support for updating WTO
sections.summary: Singapore supports efforts to update the WTO and co-launched the WTO Joint Statement Initiative on Electronic Commerce to start e-commerce rules negotiations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: We firmly support the efforts to bring the WTO up to date so that it remains well-functioning, effective and relevant.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: We co-launched the WTO Joint Statement Initiative on Electronic Commerce to kickstart negotiations for rules governing e-commerce.

sections.label: FTAs with Eurasian and Latin American blocs
sections.summary: Singapore signed an FTA with the Eurasian Economic Union last year and is negotiating FTAs with MERCOSUR and the Pacific Alliance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: For example, we signed an FTA with the Eurasian Economic Union last year and are negotiating FTAs with the Southern Common Market (MERCOSUR) and the Pacific Alliance.

sections.label: MFA helping Singaporeans abroad
sections.summary: MFA officers volunteered to fly to Wuhan to bring Singaporeans home during COVID-19, and embassies and consulates assisted Singaporeans in China and Tokyo.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: Minister Vivian Balakrishnan shared how MFA officers volunteered to fly into Wuhan to bring our fellow Singaporeans home during the COVID-19 outbreak.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: Colleagues in our Embassy in Beijing and our Consulates-General in Chengdu, Guangzhou, Shanghai and Xiamen have worked day and night to help Singaporeans in China during this period.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: Our Embassy in Tokyo assisted five Singaporeans who were on board the Diamond Princess cruise ship docked at Yokohama.

sections.label: Consular officers at Hong Kong airport
sections.summary: Last year, at the peak of Hong Kong protests, MFA consular officers were deployed at Hong Kong airport to assist Singaporeans returning home.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: Last year, when protests in Hong Kong were at the peak, we deployed MFA consular officers at Hong Kong airport to provide consular assistance to Singaporeans wanting to return home.

sections.label: Rohingya return and ASEAN Summit
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Rohingya desire to return for an independent assessment can be discussed at the upcoming ASEAN Summit to resolve the stalemate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: I understand the camps are ready and the reception area is ready as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: But I think there is an issue of trust here and that is why the Rohingas want to go back themselves to do an independent assessment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: I am just wondering whether this can at least be discussed or put up as a topic in the agenda for the upcoming ASEAN Summit so that we can finally resolve this stalemate and move forward on this issue.

sections.label: Security concerns for Rohingya return
sections.summary: Members are concerned about their own security, and Singapore will work with ASEAN partners to make the situation conducive for return.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: But as Members are well aware of, it is also their concern about their own security and we have to make sure that the security is made available and they feel secure enough to go back.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: We will continue to work with our ASEAN partners to ensure that the situation is conducive enough for them to return.

sections.label: Allowing Rohingya independent assessment
sections.summary: The speaker appreciates ASEAN and MFA assurance but suggests allowing some Rohingya to return, assess, and tell the 1.2 million refugees in Bangladesh it is safe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: I really do appreciate all the work that ASEAN and MFA are doing by providing a lot of assurance to the Rohingyas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: But I think it would help if we just allow some of them to go back, do their own assessments and then they can tell the rest of the 1.2 million refugees in Bangladesh now that it is safe to return.
